title: Defined conditions for long-term expansion of murine and human alveolar epithelial stem cells in three-dimensional cultures
protocol: Harvest murine lung.
Sacrifice the mouse using method approved by the local Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
Spray the exposed side of the mouse with 70% ethanol.
Make an incision in the skin from the abdomen to neck using clean scissors.
Tear skin with forceps to expose subcutaneous tissue from the neck to the abdomen.
Cut abdominal muscle to expose liver and move liver and intestine to expose diaphragm.
Carefully cut through diaphragm, lateral extreme of left and right rib cage, remove sternum, and rib cages to expose heart and lungs.
Cut through renal artery.
Perfuse lung using a 10 ml syringe with a 25G needle by injecting sterile PBS through the right ventricle until lung turns pale.
Remove heart tissue.
Cut away salivary glands covering trachea.
Carefully cut thin muscle lining the trachea to expose trachea.
Put a ∼ five cm-long nylon string under the trachea using forceps and tie a knot with string to secure needle and trachea together firmly.
Insert 22G needle into trachea.
Slowly inflate lung by injecting 1 ml of digestion solution with 1 ml syringe.
Remove needle from trachea.
Tie a knot with string around the trachea.
Remove lung from mouse and transfer to a 10 cm dish.
Separate each lobe of the lung and remove connective tissue.
Mince the lung lobes into 1–2 mm³ pieces with a single edge blade (No.9).
Transfer minced lung pieces to a 15 mL tube with 2 mL of warm digestion solution using a P1000 pipet with its tip cut.
Rinse the dish with 1 mL of digestion solution to collect any residual tissue pieces, and combine them with the collected tissue in step b.
Incubate the sample at 37°C for 20 min with constant and horizontal rotation at approximately 10 rpm.
Vigorously mix samples with a P1000 pipette approximately 30 times in a tissue culture hood.
Return the sample to a 37°C incubator and continue incubation for an additional 15 min with constant rotation.
Vigorously mix samples with a P1000 pipette approximately 30 times in a tissue culture hood after the initial 20-minute incubation period.
Connect a 100 μm cell strainer to a reducing adapter and place it on a 15 mL tube.
Wet the cell strainer with 1 mL of 10% FBS in DMEM/F12 containing anti-anti.
Transfer the cell suspension to the cell strainer for filtration, allowing cells to drain into the tube.
Rinse the cell strainer with 10 mL of 10% FBS in DMEM/F12 to stop the enzymatic reaction.
Collect any residual cell suspension from the bottom side of the cell strainer using a P1000 pipet.
Centrifuge the tube at 400 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Add 2 mL of Red Blood Cell lysis buffer to the sample.
Resuspend the pellet by pipetting.
Incubate for 2 min at 20°C–25°C.
Stop RBC lysis with 10 mL of 10% FBS in DMEM/F12 containing anti-anti.
Pass the cell suspension through a 40 μm cell strainer into a 50 mL tube.
Wash the cell strainer with 10 mL of 10% FBS in DMEM/F12.
Centrifuge the tube at 400 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of 2% FBS in DMEM/F12 and transfer to a 1.5 mL tube.
Dilute the antibodies in 200 μL of DMEM/F12 containing 2% FBS.
Mix EpCAM/CD326-Brilliant Violet 711 at a ratio of 1:200 with the diluted antibodies.
Mix Lysotracker-Green DND-26 at a ratio of 1:10000 with the diluted antibodies.
Mix CD140a-PE at a ratio of 1:200 with the diluted antibodies.
Mix CD31/CD45-eFluor 450 at a ratio of 1:200 with the diluted antibodies.
Resuspend cell pellet in the tube containing diluted antibodies.
Cover the tube with aluminum foil and incubate for 30 min at 4°C with constant horizontal rotation at 8 rpm.
Centrifuge the tube at 400 g at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Wash cells twice with 1 mL of 2% FBS in DMEM/F12.
After each wash, centrifuge the tube at 400 g at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Resuspend the cell pellet with 1 mL of 2% FBS in DMEM/F12.
Equilibrate the 35 μm filter of a FACS cell collection tube with 0.5 mL of 2% FBS in DMEM/F12 before adding the single-cell suspension.
Wash the filter with 500 μL of 2% FBS in DMEM/F12 and place the tube on ice.
Sort cells on a FACS machine using the gating strategy shown in Figure 2.
Collect the sorted AT2 cells in 2% FBS in DMEM/F12.
Mince human lung tissue after removing pleura, airways, large veins, and arteries.
Dissociate minced lung tissue to create a single-cell suspension.
Purify human alveolar epithelial type 2 cells using magnet-activated cell sorting (MACS).
Prepare the digestion solution (Collagenase type I: 450 units/mL, Dispase: 5 units/mL, DNase I: 10 units/mL).
Incubate the digestion solution at 37°C prior to use.
Take a piece of lung and remove the pleura by pulling with forceps.
Cut approximately 3 g of human lung tissue and move to a 10 cm petri dish.
Dissect out and discard airways, large veins, and arteries from the lung tissue.
Mince the lung chunks into small (1–2 mm³) pieces using a single edge blade (No.9).
Transfer minced lung pieces to a P1000 pipet tip with its tip cut off.
Transfer the lung pieces to a 50 mL tube containing 14 mL of warm digestion solution.
Rinse the petri dish with 1 mL of digestion solution to collect any residual tissue pieces and add them to the tube.
Incubate the sample at 37°C for 1 hour with constant horizontal rotation at approximately 10 rpm.
Mix the samples rigorously using a P1000 pipette about 30 times under the tissue culture hood every 15 minutes.
Set up two 100 μm cell strainers on 50 mL tubes.
Wet the cell strainer with 5 mL of 10% FBS in DMEM/F12 containing anti-anti.
Pipette approximately 7.5 mL of cell suspension onto each cell strainer.
Rinse the sample with an additional 20 mL of 10% FBS in DMEM/F12 containing anti-anti.
Centrifuge the tubes at 450 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Collect the supernatant into fresh tubes and repeat centrifugation.
Resuspend the pellet from step j in 2 mL red blood cell lysis buffer.
Incubate for 2 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
If starting lung tissue has a high number of blood cells, extend red blood cell lysis buffer incubation to 5 minutes.
Stop RBC lysis with 10 mL of 10% FBS in DMEM/F12 containing anti-anti.
Perform the red blood cell lysis on pellet from step k and stop the lysis with 10 mL of 10% FBS in DMEM/F12 containing anti-anti.
Filter the sample through a 40 μm cell strainer.
Combine samples from step m and n.
Centrifuge the combined cell suspension at 450 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of 2% FBS in DMEM/F12.
Transfer the resuspended cells to a 1.5 mL tube.
Perform magnet-activated cell sorting according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Centrifuge and resuspend the cell pellet in 500 μL of MACS buffer (1% BSA, 2 mM EDTA in PBS containing 1% anti-anti - sterile filtered with a 0.22 μm filter).
Store the MACS buffer at 4°C for up to 3–4 weeks.
Add 10 μl of blocking reagent TruStain FcX and incubate at 4°C for 15 min.
Add 500 μL of MACS buffer, centrifuge at 450 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Wash the pellet with 1 ml of MACS buffer and centrifuge at 450 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Add 5 μl of HTII-280 mouse IgM antibody, resuspend the pellet in 300 μL of MACS buffer, and incubate at 4°C for 1 h with horizontal rotation at 8 rpm.
Wash the pellet with 1 ml of MACS buffer and centrifuge at 450 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Dilute secondary anti-mouse IgM-magnetic beads at a ratio of 1:10 in 300 μL of MACS buffer.
Resuspend the cell pellet with diluted magnetic beads and incubate for 30 minutes at 4°C with horizontal rotation at 8 rpm.
Add 1 mL of MACS buffer to the mixture, then centrifuge at 450 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Wash the cell pellet with 1 mL of MACS buffer by centrifugation at 450 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 500 μL MACS buffer.
Set up a MACS separator equipped with an LS column in a tissue culture hood and equilibrate the LS column with 3 mL of MACS buffer, discarding the flow-through.
Apply the resuspended sample to the LS column and discard the flow-through after application.
Wash the LS column three times with 3 mL of MACS buffer each time.
Add 5 mL of MACS buffer to the LS column, plunge immediately, and collect the flow-through in a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the collected flow-through at 450 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend the pellet from the centrifuged flow-through in 500 μL of SFFF medium.
Count the number of cells after resuspension.
Thaw matrigel aliquots at 4°C approximately 5-7 hours prior to use.
Centrifuge the cell suspension (from FACS or MACS) at 4°C and 450 g for 10 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant and suspend the cell pellet in 500 μL of advanced DMEM/F12.
Count cells using a hemocytometer or automated cell counter.
Take 10 μL of cell suspension.
Mix with 10 μL of 0.4% trypan blue solution.
Place coverslip on a hemocytometer.
Transfer 10 μL of trypan blue/cell suspension solution between coverslip and hemocytometer base.
Count all cells in four 1 mm² corner squares.
Calculate the number of viable cells.
Plating AT2 cells in 3-dimensional matrix to generate alveolospheres.
Take 2000–3000 cells in a volume of 25 μL of culture medium.
Add the same amount of matrigel (25 μL for each droplet) to the cell suspension.
Mix gently by pipetting.
Avoid air bubbles while pipetting matrigel/cell suspension.
Pipette 50 μL of Matrigel and cell suspension to the bottom of the culture plate.
Place the plate with droplets in a 37°C incubator for 20 minutes to solidify the Matrigel.
Add 2 mL of SFFF (human AT2 cells) or AMM (mouse AT2 cells) in each well.
Change medium every 2–3 days.
Aspirate the culture medium without disrupting Matrigel droplets using a vacuum aspirator.
Add 1 mL of TrypLE select to one well of a 6-well plate.
Disrupt the Matrigel droplets using a cell lifter.
Pipette several times with P1000 and transfer the suspension to a 15 mL tube.
Incubate at 37°C for 5–7 min followed by vigorous mixing by pipetting.
Add 10 mL of 10% FBS in DMEM/F12 to stop enzymatic digestion.
Centrifuge the tube at 450 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant, resuspend the cell pellet in 500 μL of culture medium and transfer cells suspension into a fresh 1.5 mL tube.
Count the cells and set up droplets with cells described above.
Prepare freezing medium containing 10% Dimethyl Sulfoxide (DMSO), 20% FBS in DMEM/F12.
Resuspend 200,000–1 million cells in 1 mL of freezing medium.
Aliquot the cell suspension into cryogenic vials.
Place the cryogenic vials in an isopropanol-containing cryo-freezing container or an isopropanol-free container and store them for 15–18 h in a -80°C freezer.
Transfer cryogenic vials to a liquid nitrogen tank for long term storage.
Aspirate the medium from the culture well.
Wash the well with 1 mL of PBS.
Remove the PBS carefully.
Add 1–1.5 mL of 4% PFA in PBS to the well.
Incubate the plate for 1 h at 20°C–25°C.
Remove the 4% PFA from the well.
Wash the well with PBS.
Proceed to OCT embedding steps.
Optional: Store plates with fixed alveolospheres at 4°C for two weeks in PBS.
Use J-Hock side of the cell filter to gently move the matrigel droplet with alveolospheres from the bottom of the plate.
Carefully scoop the alveolospheres with matrigel.
Move the alveolospheres to the cryo mold filled with OCT.
Adjust the position of alveolospheres with the pipette tip.
Move the alveolospheres near the bottom of the mold.
Use cell lifter to scrape alveolospheres from the plate.
Tilt the plate (∼45 degrees) and collect the organoids with PBS using a P1000 pipette.
Transfer collected organoids into 1.5 mL tubes.
If some alveolospheres remain in the plate, add 200 μL of PBS to collect them.
Spin down sample at 300 g for 2 min at 4°C.
Carefully remove medium with P1000 pipette, leaving around 50 μL of solution inside the tube.
Use P200 pipette to gently move alveolospheres to cryomold filled with OCT.
Place cryomold on dry ice and wait until it solidifies (turns white).
Transfer the block to -80°C for long term storage.
Incubate human alveolospheres with 4% PFA, then collect them carefully using a wide-bore P1000 tip and pipette to the cryomold.
Cryosection the frozen sample at 8–10 μm thickness.
Collect sections on Superfrost plus slides.
Dry sections at 20°C to 25°C.
Store slides at -80°C.
Bring OCT sections to 20°C to 25°C.
Wash sections twice with PBS for 5 minutes each.
Perform antigen retrieval using 10 mM sodium citrate buffer in a water bath at 95°C for 15 minutes.
Permeabilize sections using PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 10 minutes.
Incubate with 1% BSA in PBST for 30 minutes at 20°C to 25°C.
Prepare primary antibodies dilutions in blocking buffer.
Incubate sections with primary antibodies for 2 hours at 20°C to 25°C or overnight at 4°C.
Wash slides three times with PBST.
Dilute secondary antibodies (1:500) in blocking buffer.
Incubate sections with secondary antibodies for 1 hour at 20°C to 25°C.
Wash slides three times with PBST.
Mount the slides using Fluoromount G reagent with DAPI.
